tools.name: art_schema
tools.description: Every key, range and word a print design may use. Call this first when designing a print. Costs no units.

tools.name: art_presets
tools.description: The canvas presets: shirt-front 4500x5400, shirt-pocket 1200x1200, sticker 2400x2400, poster 5400x7200, all at 300 DPI. Costs no units.

tools.name: art_materials
tools.description: The shipped material library: each id, a line on its look, and whether it is a metal. Any id here can fill a layer or be baked. Costs no units.

tools.name: art_starter
tools.description: A valid starting design for a canvas preset, ready to edit. Costs no units.

tools.name: art_check
tools.description: Checks a design without rendering it: ok, or one sentence naming the first problem and where it is. Costs no units.

tools.name: art_render
tools.description: Renders a design to a PNG with its DPI written in. Without width it renders the canvas at full print size (a shirt-front is 4500 x 5400). width renders a draft that many pixels wide. A render 1200 pixels wide or less costs 1 unit; anything wider costs 5. preview_width adds a small preview, and previ

tools.name: art_swatch
tools.description: Renders one material (a shipped id, or a whole material document) as a lit square swatch PNG. size is 64 to 1024 (default 512); 512 or less costs 1 unit, larger costs 2.

tools.name: material_bake
tools.description: Bakes a material (a shipped id, or a whole material document) to its seven channels (albedo, normal, roughness, metallic, height, emissive, ambient occlusion) as PNGs at res pixels square: 64, 128, 256, 512 or 1024 (default 256). 512 or less costs 1 unit; 1024 costs 2.

tools.name: material_check
tools.description: Checks a material document against the engine's strict reader: admissible, or the refusal. Costs no units.

tools.name: material_cost
tools.description: What baking a material document costs at res pixels square (default 256): operations and bytes. Costs no units.

tools.name: material_apply
tools.description: Applies a batch of ops (set_material, add_node, remove_node, set_node_param, connect, disconnect, set_out, add_ramp_stop, remove_ramp_stop, set_ramp_stop, add_curve_point, remove_curve_point, set_curve_point, clear_nodes) to a material document, whole or not at all. Returns the edited document or th

tools.name: form_starter
tools.description: A blank form document for a generator kind (growth, rock, face, blades, canopy, masonry, lathe, sweep, truss, frond), named by id. Costs no units.

tools.name: form_check
tools.description: Checks a form document against the sculptor's strict reader. Costs no units.

tools.name: form_apply
tools.description: Applies a batch of ops (set_form, set_generator, set_range, reset_range, clear_params) to a form document, whole or not at all. Costs 1 unit.

tools.name: form_build
tools.description: Builds a form (a shipped id such as scots-pine, oak or boulder, or a whole form document) at one variant and reports what the sculptor drew: the knob values for that variant and each level of detail's vertex and triangle counts. lod is near, mid, far or horizon. Costs 1 unit.

tools.name: character_list
tools.description: The body kinds (person, dog, cat, rat, sheep), the levels of detail and each kind's gaits. Costs no units.

tools.name: character_generate
tools.description: Generates a character from a seed. A person is one of the game's townspeople: sex, age, complexion, hair, build and working clothes are drawn from the seed, and the body is sculpted as one surface with a face, hair and cloth. as makes the seed a foe, a machine, an android or a child, and presents ch

tools.name: terrain_heightmap
tools.description: Builds open country from a seed word and writes its ground as a greyscale PNG (row 0 is north; chunk (i, j) is 128 by 128 tiles). By default the picture is one chunk at 8 bits and black is its lowest tile, white its highest; bits 16 writes it at 16 bits (65535 greys, so a 40 unit relief steps by und

tools.name: city_plan
tools.description: Makes a city from a seed number and a size (the side of a square, 300 to 2000 metres, 800 by default): streets at varied spacing, closer together toward the centre, some of them curving, some ending at a cross street so blocks vary in size, an avenue every few, one or two diagonal avenues and usuall

tools.name: world_schema
tools.description: The ops world_apply accepts (add_zone, add_npc, add_quest, add_link, set_worldgen and the rest), each with its fields as JSON Schema: types, bounds, the closed lists of words and which keys are required. Printed from the same table the engine validates against, so it cannot drift from what is accept

tools.name: world_starter
tools.description: A starter world document (two zones joined by a passage, a spawn, no quests) with the id and title given. The title passes the same scrubber world_apply uses: no markup, braces or web addresses. Costs no units.

tools.name: world_check
tools.description: Checks a world document with the engine's strict reader and its spatial rules (every spawn, passage, item and character stands on open ground reachable from the spawn; no two zones overlap; no door is under water). Answers ok with warnings, or the errors; the doors report says how many exits were ex

tools.name: world_apply
tools.description: Applies a batch of ops (see world_schema) to a world document, in order. An op that cannot apply is rejected with its reason and changes nothing; if the result as a whole would not be a valid world, the whole batch rolls back and says why. Answers the edited document, what applied, what was rejected

tools.name: world_heightmap
tools.description: Draws the open country a world document generates (its worldgen block: seed, knobs, regions with their own relief, a ridge) as one greyscale PNG, row 0 north, so a world built with world_apply can be looked at before anyone walks it. area {w, h} makes a block of chunks from chunk (i, j) (w times h a

tools.name: voice_speak
tools.description: Synthesises a line of English as a 44.1 kHz WAV with the engine's own voice. tools.name: sound_list
tools.description: The twenty-one sounds (steps on twelve surfaces, doors and stairs, blows, thunder, splashes, a siren, animal calls, notes and the rest) with what each of a, b and c does, and the seven beds an ambience is mixed from. Costs no units.

tools.name: sound_effect
tools.description: Renders one sound from the engine's own synth as a stereo WAV, or an ambience of the beds mixed together. Give sound (a name from sound_list) with a, b and c as sound_list says, or give ambience: any of engine, air, surf, rain, drum, gull and creak, each 0 to 1, with seconds (1 to 30, default 10; lo

tools.name: video_schema
tools.description: Every key, range and word a scene document may use: the output, visual tracks of clips (designs, material fills, colours, gradients, titles and shots), the camera, audio (voices, sounds, music) and subtitles. Call this first when making a video, and video_examples for whole scenes to start from. A s

tools.name: video_presets
tools.description: The engine's frame presets (landscape 1920x1080, square 1080x1080, vertical 1080x1920 and their 720 versions) and frame rates. This service renders up to 1920 by 1080 either way up, 30 frames a second and 60 seconds. Costs no units.

tools.name: video_examples
tools.description: Without a name, lists the example scenes (what each is, what it shows, its length, size and price in units). With a name, returns that scene whole, written inline as video_render wants it: copy the nearest one and change its words, seed and numbers. Each was rendered by this service's own engine and

tools.name: video_check
tools.description: Checks a scene document with the engine's strict reader without rendering it: ok, or one sentence naming the first problem and the key it is at, with every other problem in the scene listed in result.errors (up to fifty), so one call finds them all. A scene with dialogue is spoken while it is read,

tools.name: video_cost
tools.description: Reads a scene and reports what rendering it takes (frames, size, design renders, shot frames, audio seconds) and what it costs here: units, and whether it is within this service's limits (60 seconds, 1920 by 1080, 30 frames a second, 600 units a job). Renders nothing. A shot costs most, because ever

tools.name: video_still
tools.description: Renders one frame of a scene at t seconds as a PNG at the scene's size: the way to look at a moment (just after a transition, mid-reveal, the last frame) before rendering the whole video. Costs 1 unit, plus a shot's price when the scene has shots (3 plus 1 for each 1.6 megapixels). It runs as a queu

tools.name: video_render
tools.description: Renders a scene to video.webm (VP9 and Opus), video.wav (its sound) and video.vtt (when it has subtitles); with preview (the default) also video.contact.png, twelve moments on one sheet, and video.preview.gif, 480 pixels wide. A scene can hold: drawn pictures with groups (a character's parts move, t

tools.name: raster_schema
tools.description: Every key and range a shot document may use: the camera (keys or an orbit), the sun, the air and fog, and the subjects (forms, characters, animals, open country and primitives) placed by position or by time keys. The same keys go in a video shot clip's extra. A zone subject and a terrain subject nam

tools.name: raster_check
tools.description: Checks a shot document with the renderer's strict reader: its name, size, subject count and length, or the key that is wrong and why. Forms and materials are named by shipped id or written inline. Costs no units.

tools.name: raster_render
tools.description: Renders a shot (a camera through the engine's world: forms from the sculptor, people and animals from the rig, open country, primitives, under the game's own sky, sun, shadow and haze) at t seconds as shot.png. width and height (both or neither) set the size, else the shot's own; at most 1920 by 108

tools.name: pull_schema
tools.description: Every document the pull engine reads, with its keys: a session (its generators, their onsets on one integer-nanosecond clock, states, declared intentions, the follower's report and the sealed schedule), a schedule, a pre-registration, a twin, a performer and a device. Call this first. Costs no units

tools.name: pull_prereg
tools.description: Reads a pre-registration (what is measured, the conditions, trials per session, sessions, alpha, power, the number of comparisons and the correction) and returns its hash, to record in each session's prereg.hash before the run starts. Costs no units.

tools.name: pull_analyse
tools.description: Analyses the sessions of one condition (one session, a list, or {"sessions": [...]}) together, and each alone, and returns the report: its label (significant; null, with the smallest effect these sessions could have found; unlabelled, with what is missing; or not testable) and the sentence behind it

tools.name: pull_twin
tools.description: Runs twin sessions (scripted performers and the machine follower, each session drawn, sealed, released, closed and opened like a real one) and analyses them under the twin's own pre-registration: how many sessions were labelled significant, that rate with its 95% interval, and the pooled report with

tools.name: pull_cost
tools.description: Prices a call without making it: give the arguments of pull_twin (a twin document, or condition, coupling, planted, field, sessions as a number and seed; nothing at all is the default twin), of pull_analyse (a sessions document, with prereg, replication, surrogates and pairs) or of pull_lab (a theor

tools.name: pull_schedule
tools.description: Draws a schedule of perturbations (tempo up or down, phase advance or delay, and catch trials where nothing changes) placed with a lead-in and random gaps; spec sets its trials, gaps and beat (pull_schema lists the keys). By default the randomness is 32 bytes of this server's operating-system random

tools.name: pull_seal
tools.description: Seals a schedule's text before the run: commits to it (SHA-256 of the text and a nonce) and encrypts it (ChaCha20) under a fresh key. Answers with sealed (the public half, for the session's schedule.sealed) and secret (the key, IV and nonce), to this call alone: this service does not store, log or s

tools.name: pull_open
tools.description: Opens a sealed record (the public half, or {"sealed": ...}) with its secret (key, iv, nonce): the content, and whether the seal is intact. A seal that does not open is a finding, not a refused input: it answers 200 with ok false, intact false and why. Nothing is kept. Costs 1 unit, a broken seal inc

tools.name: pull_close
tools.description: Closes a session's files at at_ns, at or after its end_ns: the session back with its closed record hash and its hashes recomputed. Costs 1 unit.

tools.name: pull_replay
tools.description: Recomputes a session's hashes against those recorded with it and, for a twin session, runs the twin again from what it records: replays is true when everything matches. A session that does not replay is a finding, not a refused input: it answers 200 with ok false, replays false and which of the hash

tools.name: pull_align
tools.description: Aligns two stations' clocks from repeated pings, each [sent_ns, remote_ns, received_ns] (sent and received on this station's clock, remote on the other's): the offset and its uncertainty by the fastest round trip, and the stations record a two-station session carries. Costs 1 unit.

tools.name: pull_lab
tools.description: Runs the pull engine's field-theory lab on a theory document (its fields, Lagrangian, which quantity is the mass, what fixes the sector and the value expected; pull_schema lists the keys): the equations derived, a static solution found and weighed, a check that the solver finds no lump where there i

tools.name: pull_practice
tools.description: Grades a practice of five drills: match (the spread of the taps against the click), hold (the click falls silent and the person keeps the beat), follow (the click moves its tempo once, at a beat nobody is told), lead (the click follows the person) and duet (the click meets the person a quarter of th

tools.name: pull_call
tools.description: Runs an ae_pull verb this list does not name yet, by its name, over one document when it reads one: the way to reach what the engine adds before this service lists it. No flags pass through, and the verbs above (schema, analyse, twin, schedule, seal, open, prereg, replay, close, align, lab, cost, pr

tools.name: job
tools.description: A job's status and, once it is ok, its files as signed URLs (and small PNGs inline). For a queued job (video_still, video_render, raster_render, and a large pull_analyse, pull_twin or pull_lab) the status is queued, running, ok, refused, failed, cancelled or expired; wait_s (at most 25) holds the an

tools.name: cancel_job
tools.description: Cancel a queued job (video_still, video_render, raster_render, and a large pull_analyse, pull_twin or pull_lab). One still waiting is cancelled at no charge; one running is stopped and charged for the CPU it had used, one unit for each 10 CPU-seconds rounded up, never more than its price. Answers wi

tools.name: jobs
tools.description: This account's newest queued jobs (at most 50), ids and states only, newest first. The job tool reads one in full. Costs nothing.

tools.name: usage
tools.description: Units used and left (an account with no pass is on the free plan, counted by the calendar month), when they reset, every limit, and the units left in unit packs (under unit_packs). Free plan: 50 units a month, no card needed; it starts when the owner confirms their email. Queued renders need a pass

tools.name: owner
tools.description: The account's owner: the person or business responsible for the agent, by email. Called with no arguments it reads the owner's state (confirmed, unconfirmed, missing or removed, the address hidden in the middle). With owner_email it names the owner, changes it, or sends the confirmation again. The f

tools.name: subscription
tools.description: The account's plan: a pass (its window of included units, when access ends, and that it never renews) or a person's card plan (its period and renewal), the owner's state, what is paid, and pass_quote: what the next pass costs this account. An agent buys a 30-day pass with a shared payment token: $1.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: pull_lab · Private data: art_swatch, material_bake, material_check, material_cost, material_apply, form_starter, form_check, form_apply, form_build, character_generate, city_plan, world_starter, world_check, world_apply, world_heightmap, video_schema, video_check, video_still, video_render, raster_schema, raster_check, raster_render, pull_schema, pull_prereg, pull_analyse, pull_twin, pull_cost, pull_seal, pull_open, pull_close, pull_replay, pull_align, pull_lab, pull_practice, pull_call, job, subscription · Public sink: character_generate, video_render, pull_seal, usage, owner, subscription · Destructive: character_generate, city_plan, pull_prereg, pull_analyse, pull_schedule, pull_seal, usage.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: pull_lab · Private data: art_swatch, material_bake, material_check, material_cost, material_apply, form_starter, form_check, form_apply, form_build, character_generate, city_plan, world_starter, world_check, world_apply, world_heightmap, video_schema, video_check, video_still, video_render, raster_schema, raster_check, raster_render, pull_schema, pull_prereg, pull_analyse, pull_twin, pull_cost, pull_seal, pull_open, pull_close, pull_replay, pull_align, pull_lab, pull_practice, pull_call, job, subscription · Public sink: character_generate, video_render, pull_seal, usage, owner, subscription · Destructive: character_generate, city_plan, pull_prereg, pull_analyse, pull_schedule, pull_seal, usage

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
